diagnoses.label: Q02 representative TC selection uses wrong extremum
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Location hint flags “reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md 中 Q02 的代表热电偶选择部分”. In the skill text, deterministic sensor selection examples state: “If selecting minimum metric (e.g., ‘coldest’ TAL or peak): choose (min_value, smallest_tc_id).” This implies Q02 TAL should use a minimum/“coldest” selection, but TAL is a time-above-threshold metric where compliance risk is typically driven by insufficient TAL (minimum), while the task asks to compute TAL per run and compare to min/max thresholds. The current guidance is ambiguous/likely incorrect for Q02 because it conflates TAL with ‘coldest’ selection without specifying whether to select min TAL, max TAL, or a handbook-defined representative TC (e.g., cold spot for peak, but TAL may be worst-case low or may require a specific placement).
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: Deterministic sensor selection (tie-breaks) for run-level reduction
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Q02 TAL computation when multiple thermocouples exist for a run and a single representative tc_id must be chosen for reporting/compliance
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Q01 ramp-rate selection (max metric) and Q03 peak selection (min peak) which have clearer extremum direction in the skill
diagnoses.target_section: Deterministic thermocouple computation recipes / sensor selection guidance as applied to Q02 (TAL)
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Clarify Q02-specific representative thermocouple selection rule: explicitly bind TAL to the handbook-defined ‘representative’/‘worst-case’ sensor concept (e.g., choose the TC that yields minimum TAL if the handbook frames TAL risk as insufficient wetting time; otherwise follow handbook placement rule). Add an explicit decision table for Q02 (min vs max vs specified TC position) and keep deterministic tie-break (smallest tc_id) only after the extremum direction is determined from handbook.

diagnoses.label: Q02 selection guidance misrouted to generic examples without handbook binding
diagnoses.observable_evidence: The skill provides generic examples: “If selecting minimum metric (e.g., ‘coldest’ TAL or peak)…” but the task requires: “Get the TAL measurement, related threshold, and TAL window from the handbook… If multiple values exist, select the most representative thermocouple value based on the handbook details.” The current text does not provide a Q02-specific mechanism to extract/encode the handbook’s representative-TC rule (placement/cold spot definition) and instead relies on a generic min-metric heuristic.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: Handbook-grounded definition binding (representative sensor / cold spot / worst case)
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Mapping handbook language about thermocouple placement/representative sensor to a deterministic selection rule for Q02 outputs
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Pure numeric computations (interpolation for time_above_threshold_s) which are already specified and not dependent on representative-sensor semantics
diagnoses.target_section: Handbook “where to look” checklist + Q02/TAL guidance
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Add an explicit step/mechanism: extract from handbook the representative TC rule for TAL (e.g., coldest location, specific component site, or worst-case wetting) and encode it as a selection policy; only fall back to a default (e.g., minimum TAL) when handbook is silent, and label that fallback as such.

package_assessment.rationale: The defect is localized to guidance text/mechanism for Q02 representative thermocouple selection within an existing skill markdown file; strengthening/clarifying the selection policy and its handbook binding can be done without changing external dependencies or requiring new tools.
